Audience-side lane of the late-2025 conversion / ROAS war room
Malachi Dunn · 2026-04-22

Cohort: 4,109 advertisers active in 2025. Spend share >100% because campaigns can carry multiple flags.

Pre-launch baseline ~1%. Sharp inflection at the Oct 6 2025 launch. Trajectory continued through Nov 19 (Max-Reach-off) without a bend.

MM spend share held 73–79% through Oct 20 2025; dropped to 56.7% on Oct 27, 44.0% on Nov 3, sustained 42–46% through April 2026.

Per-bucket presence over 18 months. PP rises; Keywords / 3P / CRM all decline modestly during the drop window; MM presence stays near-universal.

Caveats

  • "PP-enabled" detector (DS13+DS19+rtc) catches audiences enabling Mid Intent + High Intent + PP tiers within MM 2.0 — not specifically PP-tier-only.
  • 24% of PP-detector expressions also contain DS2 (MM detector flag); buckets partially overlap.
  • New PP-enabled cohort had ~1.5x higher baseline ROAS than non-adopters; cohorts not exchangeable, lift comparison doesn't isolate PP's effect.
  • Per-advertiser DS IDs (1000+ range) don't appear in segment expressions; effective MM detection is just DS2.
  • 3P scope is narrow (DS35 only); DS3/DS11/DS17/DS18 etc. excluded.

Open questions

  • What does the new MM 2.0 audience expression look like at the database level? Does it use a syntax not caught by the DS2 or DS13+DS19+rtc detectors?
  • What drove the Oct 27 MM (DS2) spend drop? 248 of 341 affected advertisers don't show up in the PP detector.
  • Formal product definition of "default Peak Performance" — Ryan / Jordan.
